title: The Open Wreck
premise: Zephyrine Yarrow, a nomadic salvage diver haunted by the wreck her late father helped sink, takes a contract off a monsoon-battered coast where the navy forbids questions. When an unprecedented low tide exposes a sea cave holding a sealed expedition vault, Zephyrine and her ragtag crew discover evidence that her father's 'accident' was a cover-up — and that someone in their own crew is reporting to the navy. Racing the monsoon, they must recover the truth, decide what to reveal and what to bury with the dead, and get home alive. In the end, Zephyrine chooses loyalty to her father's memory over the whole truth, scuttles the proof, and finally stops running.
about_author: Oscar Okonkwo is a former maritime surveyor who spent six years charting wrecks along West African and Southeast Asian coasts before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people who work the sea's margins, where salvage is livelihood and silence is currency.

chapters.title: Ballast
chapters.summary: Zephyrine Yarrow's POV. Working a routine salvage job, she gets word the navy has flagged her next contract zone as restricted — the same waters where her father died twenty years ago. She takes the job anyway because rent is due and stopping costs more. Emotional beat: restless defiance masking grief.

chapters.title: The Tide That Lied
chapters.summary: Crew POV through deckhand Marisol. An impossible low tide drains the bay, revealing a cave mouth no chart admits exists. Inside: rusted dive gear stamped with her father's company logo. The crew argues about whether to report it. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Admission
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Legends say the cave charges admission; they descend anyway and find a sealed vault from a 1990s government expedition, logs intact. Her father's name appears on the manifest — listed as crew, not casualty. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering your childhood was a lie.

chapters.title: Company Man
chapters.summary: Engineer Teodor's POV. A navy patrol boat circles the bay asking questions. Teodor, hiding his own debts, notices someone aboard has been transmitting coordinates. Suspicion falls on quiet navigator Ash. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening like a winch cable.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A deep dive recovers her father's personal logbook: the expedition found something the navy wanted buried, and he was ordered to sink the evidence — with himself as part of the price. Emotional beat: fury and tenderness colliding.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Storm trackers confirm landfall in five days. The navy issues a final evacuation order that would seal the cave forever. The crew must choose: flee with nothing or stay for one last dive. Emotional beat: solidarity forged under deadline.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Tide
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Revealed: Ash has been feeding the navy since they threatened her family — but she's been stalling them, buying the crew time. Confronted at gunpoint by a navy boarding party, she helps Zephyrine escape into the cave system. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Pressure
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Climax begins: a storm surge traps Zephyrine inside the collapsing cave with the vault's final record — footage proving the navy sank its own expedition. Her air runs low as she chooses between saving the proof and saving herself. Emotional beat: claustrophobic moral crisis.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Full-crew POV rotation during the monsoon's peak. They fight the boat out of the harbor as the cave floods shut forever, the evidence lost — or so the navy believes. Ash goes ashore to face her handlers alone. Emotional beat: exhausted triumph shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: Anchorage
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Weeks later, she pays off the crew and, for the first time, signs a lease instead of leaving town. She keeps one page of her father's logbook and burns the rest, choosing memory over proof. Emotional beat: stillness earned — the diver who finally stops moving.
